question: A 29-year-old primigravid woman at 24 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for a prenatal visit. She feels well. She has no personal history of serious illness. Medications include iron supplements and a multivitamin. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F) and blood pressure is 108/60 mm Hg. Pelvic examination shows a uterus consistent in size with a 24-week gestation. A 1-hour 50-g glucose challenge shows a glucose concentration of 155 mg/dL (N < 135 mg/dL). A 100-g oral glucose tolerance test shows glucose concentrations of 205 mg/dL (N < 180 mg/dL) and 154 mg/dL (N <140 mg/dL) at 1 and 3 hours, respectively. She refuses treatment with insulin. Which of the following complications is her infant at greatest risk of developing at birth?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Gestational diabetes" -> "elevated maternal blood glucose levels" -> "increased fetal exposure to glucose" -> "fetal hyperinsulinemia" -> "increased risk of macrosomia" -> "increased risk of birth complications" -> "intrauterine growth restriction" -> 80% CHAIN: "Gestational diabetes" -> "poorly controlled maternal hyperglycemia" -> "increased risk of fetal hyperglycemia" -> "increased risk of neonatal hypoglycemia" -> "hyperglycemia in the infant" -> "risk of hyperglycemia at birth" -> "hyperglycemia" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The infant of the woman with gestational diabetes is at greatest risk of developing intrauterine growth restriction due to the increased fetal exposure to glucose leading to fetal hyperinsulinemia and subsequent risk of macrosomia and birth complications.
analysis: The core medical principle here is the increased risk of intrauterine growth restriction in infants of mothers with gestational diabetes due to fetal hyperinsulinemia from increased glucose exposure. This can lead to macrosomia and birth complications. While other complications like hypocalcemia, omphalocele, hypermagnesemia, and hyperglycemia can occur, the greatest risk for this infant is intrauterine growth restriction.
